History:
- Main complaints: recurrent severe frontal headaches, episodic shortness of breath while seated at work, palpitations (heart “beating fast”), bilateral hand tingling, reduced appetite with ~5 lb unintentional weight loss, and decreased libido.
- Onset/duration: Symptoms began after changing jobs; occur intermittently, often during work (meetings/computer use), not on commute. No prior history of similar headaches.
- Headache details: Frontal, non-radiating, occurs mainly at work; sometimes mild nausea; no clear prodrome.
- Dyspnea: Occurs at rest while sitting at desk; not with exercise.
- Palpitations: About once daily or more.
- Tingling: “Quick pricking” sensation in both hands; legs not involved.
- Weight/appetite: Decreased appetite; ~5 lb unintentional weight loss; clothes not noticeably looser; no outside comments on weight change.
- Psychosocial: Work stress rated 7–8/10; law firm environment; extensive reading/computer use; symptoms temporally associated with job change.

Past Medical History:
- Hyperthyroidism (patient-reported; see conflict below).
- Medications: Thyroxine (dose/route/frequency not documented). Conflict noted with stated diagnosis.
- Allergies: Not documented.
- Social history: Alcohol ~once weekly, “a couple of glasses of wine.” No tobacco. No recreational drugs.

Physical Examination:
- Telehealth visit; no in-person exam performed.
- No shortness of breath with exercise (per history).

Impression:
- Undifferentiated episodic symptoms (headache, palpitations, dyspnea at rest, bilateral hand paresthesias, decreased appetite/weight, reduced libido) temporally associated with job change and high stress; known thyroid disease. No definitive diagnosis made on call; requires in-person assessment and thyroid testing.

Management Plan:
- Arrange in-person clinic appointment (patient to book via app).
- Perform physical examination with focus on cardiovascular and respiratory systems.
- Obtain blood tests to assess thyroid status (“thyroxine/thyroid tests” as discussed).
- Defer starting any new medication until after in-person evaluation.

Patient Summary:
- 35-year-old lawyer with new-onset, intermittent headaches and autonomic/paresthetic symptoms mainly during work since changing jobs. High stress reported; has thyroid disease and is on thyroxine. Plan is in-person evaluation and thyroid blood tests before initiating treatment.

Key Takeaways:
- Book and attend in-person clinic appointment.
- Expect heart and lung exam and thyroid-related blood tests.
- No medications will be started until after the in-person review.

Next Steps:
- Schedule clinic visit via app.
- Complete ordered thyroid labs at/after visit per clinician direction.
- Follow up with results and management plan after examination.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: Allergy status; detailed headache characterization (onset per episode, duration, severity scale, photophobia/phonophobia, aura, neck stiffness), full ROS, vitals, neurologic exam, mental health screening, medication dose/route/frequency, family history.
- Internal conflicts: Initial triage noted “feeling hot,” but patient did not endorse and instead described intermittent shortness of breath; conflict noted. Patient reports “hyperthyroidism” but medication listed is thyroxine (typically used for hypothyroidism); conflict noted. Age vs DOB partially unclear (stated age 35; DOB verbalized as “October 7, ninety-three something”); conflict noted.
- Transcript quality: Intermittently fragmented/inaudible with some incomplete responses; limits precision of symptom characterization.
